Fire Safety Inspection

Know what needs fixing before the authorities tell you.

JMB / MC & building managersShoplot & factory ownersBefore a BOMBA inspection
8Areas Checked
100%Photo Evidence
3Urgency Levels
0Repairs Sold
4 photosCommercial & Asset

We inspect and document the condition of your building's fire safety provisions — escape routes, fire doors, extinguishers, hose reels, detection, emergency lighting and fire-rated compartmentation — and report what we find with photographic evidence. This is a condition inspection and documentation service. It is not a BOMBA certification and not a compliance approval; what it gives you is a clear, evidence-backed picture of what needs attention before an official inspection.

What's included

  • Escape routes — obstruction, width and access
  • Fire doors — installation, self-closers, damage, seals
  • Fire extinguishers — presence, placement, service date
  • Hose reels & hydrants — access and physical condition
  • Smoke detection & alarm system — presence and placement
  • Emergency lighting & EXIT signage — presence and condition
  • Compartmentation — unsealed service penetrations through fire-rated walls
  • Fire appliance access — unobstructed approach routes

Instruments we use

SIRIM Calibrated
Laser DistanceThermal CameraMeasuring Tape

What you receive

  • Condition report with photographic evidence for every finding
  • Findings ranked by urgency, so you know what to fix first
  • A clear note of what falls outside our scope and needs a registered competent person

Why It Matters

Find the Gaps Before an Official Inspection Does

Evidence, Not Opinion

Every finding carries a photograph and a location, so nothing is a matter of argument

Ranked by Urgency

You know what must be fixed now and what can wait, so the budget goes to the right place

Honest About Our Limits

Anything requiring a registered competent person is named as such — we do not pretend otherwise

A Record You Can Hand Over

A written condition report for your committee, your owner or your insurer

Useful for JMB and MC

Turns a vague worry into a funded, scheduled list of works

We Do Not Sell the Fix

We do not supply or install fire equipment, so there is nothing for us to over-specify

How It Works

4 Stages of a Fire Safety Inspection

A walk-through, a record, and a prioritised list you can act on

1

Scope & Building Review

We agree the areas to cover and review any drawings or past reports you have

2

On-Site Walk-Through

Every escape route, door, appliance and service penetration is checked and photographed

3

Findings Recorded & Ranked

Each item is logged with its location, photograph and urgency level

4

Report & Walk-Through With You

We hand over the report and go through it, so your team knows exactly what to action first

Inspection Scope

6 Areas Where Problems Are Usually Found

These are the items that most often fail on the day it matters

Escape Routes

The route out on the worst day

What We Look For
Corridors used for storageExit doors locked or blockedInsufficient widthRoute not obvious without signage
Why It Matters
A blocked route is the single most common and most dangerous finding

Fire Doors

Only work when closed

What We Look For
Self-closer removed or wedged openDamaged or missing intumescent sealsGaps too wide at the frameOrdinary door fitted in a fire-rated opening
Why It Matters
A wedged-open fire door gives the same protection as no door at all

Extinguishers & Hose Reels

Present, reachable, in date

What We Look For
Service date expiredUnit missing from its bracketBlocked by furniture or stockWrong type for the risk present
Why It Matters
Equipment nobody can reach in five seconds is equipment you do not have

Detection & Alarm

The warning that buys time

What We Look For
Detectors missing from enclosed areasUnits painted over or coveredCall points obstructedNo evidence of routine testing
Why It Matters
Detection decides how much time everyone else gets

Emergency Lighting & Signage

When the power goes

What We Look For
Fittings present but not functioningEXIT signs missing at turnsSignage obscured by later worksNo illumination on stairs
Why It Matters
In smoke and darkness, signage is the only thing people can follow

Compartmentation

The part nobody looks at

What We Look For
Pipes and cables passing through fire-rated walls unsealedHoles left after later renovation worksCeiling voids open between unitsFire-rated wall not carried to the slab above
Why It Matters
An unsealed penetration lets smoke travel the whole floor in minutes
